newsitem.title: USA: Montana nears passage of electricity restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Montana nears passage of electricity restructuring.

text.p: Montana legislation authorizing restructuring of the state's electric utility industry no later than July 1, 2002, was close to approval by the state's House of Representatives on Tuesday, Montana Power Co said Wednesday.
The legislative action yesterday marked the final debate, with a final confirming vote by House members expected later today or tomorrow, the utility said.
The measure, which was approved earlier by the Montana Senate, matches a restructuring proposal made by the utility late last year.

Under the bill, large industrial customers can choose their power supplier on July 1, 1998. After pilot programs on choice, all residential, commercial and smaller industrial customers will have choice of supplier by July 1, 2002.
The legislation also includes a two-year rate freeze, beginning July 1, 1998, and an additional two-year freeze on the energy component of bills for residential and commercial ratepayers.
The procedure for recovery of stranded costs includes a review of utility cost estimates by the Montana Public Service Commission.
The Montana Senate still will have to take action on amendments added in the House, and the bill must also be signed by the state's governor.
